subject: SLO priming: latency, streaming behavior & warm-pool actions
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Amina Noor <amina@fastpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: SLO priming: latency, streaming behavior & warm-pool actions

Hi Amina (and team),

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on FastPay's critical SLOs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a priming run scheduled: 

Recap of targets you outlined this morning:
- Endpoint latency: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 250ms (token-level generation) for typical payment-verification prompts (~220 tokens).
- Concurrency: steady-state 60 concurrent users, burst to 600 concurrent for 90s windows during payment closing cycles.
- Streaming: chunked streaming to UX (partial tokens) required; client can tolerate up to 300ms first-chunk latency but needs continuous token flow thereafter.
- Acceptable queueing/window: short queueing acceptable up to 10s at p99 during bursts if streaming starts immediately for partial results.

Key platform asks from our side:
- Can you share a 2-hour traffic sample or synthetic profile we can use? (format: timestamp, concurrent_sessions, avg_seq_len) — I attached fp_priming_profile_v1.csv with an example schema.
- Confirm whether the 600 concurrent burst is spike-and-decay (single 90s pulse) or repeated pulses across the day.
- Any regulatory constraints for keeping KV cache or prefixes between requests?

What Redwood will run for the priming run:
1) Simulation of your burst profile against two configs: hosted with autoscale + warm-pool (20 prewarmed instances) and dedicated reserved pool (no warm-pool, but higher baseline).
2) Measure p50/p95 token latency, first-byte streaming latency, and tail queueing behavior.
3) Produce a short MAP (mutual action plan) with failure-mode triggers and recommended warm-pool sizes + priming policy.

Proposed immediate next steps (action items):
- Amina: share realistic traffic sample or confirm synthetic profile by Mon 31 Aug EOD (attach if possible).
- FastPay SRE (Chris): confirm whether KV cache persistence is allowed across sessions (yes/no).
- Marissa: draft MAP and test plan based on provided sample; target internal dry-run Aug 31.
- Ben/Karthik: prep canary config & proposed warm-pool sizes (20 / 50 / 100) for the simulation.

I've attached the sample CSV schema and a one-page warm-pool diagram for context. If you want us to run a quick smoke test on a staging endpoint before the full simulation, we can do that as soon as we have the sample.

Thanks,

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0103

Attachments: fp_priming_profile_v1.csv (schema), warmpool-proposal-diagram.png
From: Amina Noor <amina@fastpay.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Dalton <chris.dalton@fastpay.com>, product@fastpay.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO priming: latency, streaming behavior & warm-pool actions

Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and attachments.

- I've attached a 2-hour sample from last week's peak (fp_sample_aug22.csv). The burst is usually a series of short pulses over ~10 minutes (we see 3x 60–90s spikes within high-load windows).
- KV cache: we do store session-level state for up to 5 minutes, but we cannot persist user PII in the cache. Non-PII prefixes are OK.
- Streaming: first-chunk latency target: <=300ms; after first chunk, we need continuous updates at ~100–250ms token cadence.

Confirming: we'll aim to have Chris join your dry-run on Aug 31. Also, we prefer Redwood to test warm-pool sizes 30 and 60 to start (we suspect 20 will be insufficient).

Attached: fp_sample_aug22.csv (traffic sample). Let us know if the format is unexpected.

—Amina
Amina Noor
Head of Product, FastPay
amina@fastpay.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amina Noor <amina@fastpay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO priming: latency, streaming behavior & warm-pool actions

Thanks Amina — file received and looks good. Short plan and scheduling notes from our ops side: 

Planned runs (internal):
- Aug 31 14:00–15:00 PT: internal dry-run against staging endpoint (simulate single 90s pulse). Goal: validate traffic ingestion and streaming hooks. Owners: Ben (test harness), Karthik (runtime config).
- Sep 1 10:00–12:00 PT: full simulation with 2-hour sample (3x pulses pattern) against two configs (hosted autoscale + warm-pool sizes 30 and 60). Goal: measure p50/p95, first-chunk latency, and p99 queueing. Owners: Marissa (MAP author), Vivek (client liaison).

Pre-run checks:
- Ben: ensure streaming test client emits first-chunk within 300ms and then token cadence options 100/200ms.
- Karthik: prepare warm-pool orchestration scripts and a fallback policy (queue-to-limit + model-variant fallback) for the test.

Deliverables post-run:
- Short readout with per-config SLO table (p50/p95/p99, first-chunk), waterfall trace for first-byte, and suggested warm-pool size + priming duration.
- MAP with canary rollout steps and rollback triggers.

Ben/Karthik: ping here when the staging harness is up and we can invite FastPay SRE to the dry-run.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-map-priming.md
From: Amina Noor <amina@fastpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Dalton <chris.dalton@fastpay.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO priming: latency, streaming behavior & warm-pool actions

Perfect — thanks for the concrete schedule. Chris will join the dry-run today at 14:00 PT. We accept testing with warm-pool sizes 30 and 60. A couple quick asks: 

- Can Redwood include a run with an enforced 10s queueing tolerance to validate the UX fallback path? We want to ensure partial streaming continues while requests queue.
- Please highlight any differences in economic impact between the two warm-pool sizes in the MAP (ballpark $$/hour).

I'll be on the call for the full simulation on Sep 1 10:00 PT. If anything changes, I will update here.

Thanks again — see you shortly.

—Amina
